policy: Saved output precision. Data transcribed from recorded notebook outputs for the presentation tables and figures; no experiment execution.

config.competitor_bid_distribution: Three independent Uniform[0, 1] bids each round
config.paired_comparisons: All main learners use the same pre-generated competitor bids; the confidence-bound ablation also uses these sequences and the same action seeds.
config.feedback: Win/reward/cost observation for the selected bid

benchmark.definition: Stochastic clairvoyant: LP chooses a fixed distribution over bids using the true expected reward and cost, with expected per-round cost <= B/T. It does not know future realized competitor bids.

metrics.realized_regret: Sum over rounds of clairvoyant expected reward per round minus realized learner utility
metrics.pseudo_regret: Sum over rounds of clairvoyant expected reward per round minus true expected reward of the selected bid
metrics.SEM: Across-trial standard deviation with ddof=1 divided by sqrt(number of trials)
metrics.ratio: Mean realized total learner reward / (clairvoyant expected per-round reward * horizon)

hard_budget.baseline: Both original agents choose the zero bid when remaining budget < 1. The largest admissible bid is 0.6; this guard is safe and conservative.
hard_budget.improved: Exclude bids greater than the remaining budget (tolerance 1e-12); the zero bid remains available. LP uses fixed initial rho, reward (v-b)*p_UCB and cost b*p_LCB.
hard_budget.kl_bound: n * KL(p_hat, q) <= log(max(t, 2)); 15 bisection iterations

confidence_bound_ablation.only_change: KL versus Hoeffding confidence interval for the same winning-probability learner

horizon_sweep.interpretation_limit: Normalized regret is not monotonic across these independent seeds/horizons. The 5000-round sweep uses a different market seed from the main experiment.

config.admissible_positive_bids: 0 < bid <= campaign valuation; zero is opt-out
config.threshold_generation: With probability 0.3 all campaigns share one uniform quantile; otherwise quantiles are independent. Apply each campaign's Beta inverse CDF, preserving the marginals.
config.paired_comparisons: Baseline, improved learner, references and ablations share market realizations and agent RNG seeds; the baseline is rerun unchanged in the improved notebook.
config.feedback: Semi-bandit feedback for played campaign/bid arms
config.auction: First-price for each campaign; win when bid >= threshold; reward (v_i-b_i)*win; cost b_i*win

benchmark.definition: Stochastic clairvoyant: true-mean LP chooses a fixed distribution over feasible super-actions with expected average cost <= B/T.
benchmark.simulated_reference_note: ClairvoyantPolicy samples the LP distribution and stops below the worst-case cost guard. Its finite-trial realized reward is distinct from the expected LP objective.

metrics.pseudo_regret: Cumulative oracle expected per-round reward minus true expected reward of selected super-action
metrics.realized_regret: Cumulative oracle expected per-round reward minus realized learner utility
metrics.SEM: Curves use across-trial ddof=1 SEM, but numerical SEM summaries are not saved in these tables.
metrics.ratio: 100 * mean realized learner utility / (oracle expected per-round reward * horizon)

hard_budget.baseline: Combinatorial-UCB and sampled clairvoyant opt out below remaining budget 1.8, covering every possible winning cost of a super-action. Random selects only actions with sum of bids <= remaining budget.
hard_budget.improved: Restrict LP support to super-actions whose sum of bids <= remaining budget + 1e-12; use empirical expected cost b*p_hat and rho_t = remaining budget / remaining rounds. Null action is the fallback.
hard_budget.kl_bound: n * KL(p_hat, q) <= log(max(t, 3)); 12 bisection iterations

rows.algorithm: KL-UCB with empirical costs and dynamic pacing

ablations.change: KL versus Hoeffding, all other improved components retained
Empirical cost versus cost LCB, all other improved components retained

configuration.bid_grid: linspace(0,1,11), filtered to bid <= campaign value
configuration.nonstationary_sequence: Oblivious thresholds: five sinusoidal cycles over the horizon, campaign-specific phases, Gaussian noise SD 0.05, clipped to [0,1].
configuration.pairing: Baseline and calibrated PD use identical environment and PD seeds; baseline is rerun in cell 17.
configuration.feedback: Full counterfactual reward/cost vectors observed after selecting the round action.

benchmark.name: best fixed distribution in hindsight
benchmark.definition: One LP on realized sequence average reward/cost, with average cost <= B/T; evaluated as F_t dot x_star.
benchmark.metric: pseudo_regret_t = F_t dot x_star - F_t dot x_t
benchmark.proposal_caveat: x_t is the proposed distribution even when a sampled action is overridden; actual utility and spend are measured from the executed action.

main_comparison.budget_checks: Cell 14 prints violation 0.00 for every reported group and override rate 0.000 to displayed precision.
main_comparison.graph_bands: Cell 15 computes pointwise sample SEM over the 10 trials, but final numeric SEM is not stored in the tables.

algorithm_changes.normalization: Fixed bounds over full horizon; removing lambda*rho is action-independent and does not change Hedge probabilities at otherwise identical settings.
algorithm_changes.baseline_guard: Play null whenever remaining budget < maximum possible round payment.
algorithm_changes.calibrated_guard: Replace the sampled action with null if its sum of bids > remaining budget.

guard_ablation.controls: Same calibrated rates, dual update, environments and seeds; only global_stop/per_action differs.
guard_ablation.supported_conclusion: No observed benefit from the per-action guard in this ablation. Improvement is supported for rate calibration; attributing a measured gain to the guard is unsupported.

horizon_sweep.interpretation: Overall decline over tested horizons, with one small increase in nonstationary values; finite simulation evidence does not prove asymptotic sublinear regret.

configuration.threshold_draws: Independent campaign Beta draws within a stationary segment.
configuration.environment_seeds: 1000 + j, j=0..29 (SEED=23 is only used for an illustrative plot)
configuration.pairing: All methods and both versions share the same environment path per trial; matching method seeds are reused across versions.

local.name: segment-local oracle
local.definition: Separate expected reward/cost LP for each segment; each uses cost cap B/T, with Beta CDF means.

global.name: segment-global oracle
global.definition: One distribution per segment under one total expected budget B; can shift spending across segments.

benchmarks.metric: gap = deterministic cumulative expected oracle utility minus realized cumulative learner utility
benchmarks.distinction: These are expected policy LP comparators, not trajectory-wise realized optima, and differ from Stage 3's best fixed distribution on the realized sequence.

main_comparison.sem: Sample SEM over 30 trials; numeric values preserved in saved HTML table.
main_comparison.budget_check_cell15: All trial expenditures asserted <= BUDGET + 1e-9; saved output confirms budget respected in every trial.

algorithm_changes.wide_window_assumption: 500 is half the known 1000-round segment length.
algorithm_changes.ucb_changes: Empirical cost replaces cost LCB in LP; cap becomes remaining budget / remaining rounds; SW also widens window.
algorithm_changes.cusum_statistic: Two-sided cumulative deviation of each selected arm's Bernoulli win indicator from its initial reference mean; reset the affected arm and force M new reference pulls.
algorithm_changes.pd_change: Calibrated Hedge and OGD rates; both Stage 4 baseline and revised PD already use the per-action maximum-payment guard.
algorithm_changes.hard_budget_enforcement: LP assigns zero mass to bid sums exceeding remaining budget; forced UCB pulls are affordable; PD replaces unaffordable sampled actions with null.

window_ablation.controls: Revised SW uses empirical costs and dynamic pacing for both windows; environments and SW seeds paired.
window_ablation.supported_conclusion: Larger window improves recorded gap on this one fixed segmented instance; this does not establish that forgetting is generally unimportant.

cusum_diagnostics.caveat: 54 is the illustrative product 2 changes x 27 arms. Reset count is not a detection accuracy measurement; saved histogram includes resets away from true change points.
